hero.lead: Claude is the model. Atti is everything around it: the harness, the memory, the persona and the channels.

sections.title: Where it's at
paragraphs: Live on Telegram since 28 October 2026 and in use every day. It captures reminders and to-dos, keeps my calendar, sends a morning brief and writes what it learns into my personal brain. Since 5 November I can also talk to it hands-free through an iPhone Shortcut.

expanders.title: What I'm building
paragraphs: An assistant that remembers, keeps my commitments and handles the routine work of my day. Rules run before the model: "done", "snooze" and "add milk" never need an LLM, and timing is set by code, not by the model. Tools are tiered by risk, so reads and simple logs just happen. Telegram came first, then voice. A console, the phone app and hardware come later.

expanders.title: What I tried
paragraphs: I borrowed Lifebox's on-device rules for reading dates and intents, so most messages never reach a model. A small, fast model handled the rest until full agent runs took over. Memory search started as a keyword ranker with a fixed test: the right memory came first 89% of the time, and that is the score an embedding model has to beat. Every reply where Atti apologised, failed or was corrected becomes a morning review item, and each fix becomes a regression case built from the real message. Live replays rerun those cases against the real model in a sandbox.

expanders.title: What didn't work
paragraphs: The outbox gave up after about seven minutes and silently lost nudges; it now retries until a deadline. Forwarded messages triggered actions; now they are saved as notes. My early failure flags only caught apologies, so confident but wrong replies slipped through; a new flag now catches claims with nothing behind them. After a restart, old sessions repeated stale "I can't" answers; restarts now open a fresh session. When the machine logged out, Atti stopped quietly; a watchdog now notices and sends a late brief.

expanders.title: Open questions and next
paragraphs: Can a small decision model route messages faster and cheaper than a general model, at similar accuracy? That experiment is written up and has no results yet. A context engine that hands each agent only the slice of memory it needs. A builder that turns a spec Atti writes into a draft pull request: it is built, and parked until the rest is steadier. Then a console for heavier planning, Lifebox as the phone app, and hardware.
